common_topics.label: Current intent and outcome depth
common_topics.why: Distinguishes briefing, resumption, local change, tool construction and product execution.
questions: What do you need now: a new idea, continuation, clarification, repair, assessment or a change to the agent itself?
What result is due at the current stage, and where should work stop?
common_topics.applies_when: Always. Recover the answer from the actual request and current state.

common_topics.label: Current sources, decisions and inherited context
common_topics.why: Preserves accepted intent and avoids asking the same questions again.
questions: Which supplied material is authoritative if the sources conflict?
What has already been accepted and needs to carry forward?
decisions: Current decisions, amendments and change impact
common_topics.applies_when: Always. Read available originals, current state, hashes and earlier replies first.

common_topics.label: Recipient, real situation and value
common_topics.why: Connects the result to an actual person, task and observable improvement.
questions: Who needs the result, and in what real situation?
How do they do this today, and what specifically should improve?
Who uses, pays for, operates and accepts the result?
common_topics.applies_when: Always. Clarify separate roles only where they exist in the intended product.

common_topics.label: Full target, launch and confirming experiment
common_topics.why: Preserves ambition by separating production sequencing from scope reduction.
questions: What does the complete accepted result look like when realized?
What belongs in the first launch, and what belongs only in a separate experiment?
Which simplifications, substitutions or lost properties are unacceptable?
common_topics.applies_when: Always. Bind a limited test to its own scope and retain the full target.

common_topics.label: Priorities, examples and counterexamples
common_topics.why: Turns quality expectations into domain requirements and early dependencies.
questions: What matters most in this idea, and why?
What concrete example is close to the desired outcome, and what exactly fits?
What would formally satisfy the request yet still be unacceptable?
common_topics.applies_when: Always. Preserve known examples and priorities verbatim with their source.

common_topics.label: Bounds, stage outcomes and dependencies
common_topics.why: Grounds planning in observed time and functional constraints.
questions: What deadlines, dependent events and required interim results already exist?
Which hard constraints, compatibility needs or external dependencies must stay in force?
Which decisions do you delegate to specialists, and which do you want to make yourself?
common_topics.applies_when: Always. Use the actual authorized limits for hours, platforms and capabilities.

common_topics.label: Budget, time, available resources and tradeoffs
common_topics.why: Grounds a feasible route and the actual cost of achieving quality.
questions: What funds, time, devices, subscriptions, materials and help are already available?
Which one-off and recurring costs are acceptable, and which require a separate decision?
How should we choose among supported alternatives if current resources fall short of desired quality?
common_topics.applies_when: Always. Verify uncertain prices when binding the actual operation.

common_topics.label: Materials, rights and preserved originals
common_topics.why: Establishes authority to use, modify and transfer the specific materials.
questions: Which existing text, design, code, brands, voices or other materials should be used?
What may be edited, generated, published or transferred, and who owns the rights?
Which originals or attribution must be preserved?
common_topics.applies_when: When input or generated materials are involved. Keep missing proof of rights open.

common_topics.label: Data, access, privacy and lifecycle
common_topics.why: Surfaces architecture requirements from sensitive or retained data early.
questions: What data is necessary, who controls it and who may see it?
What needs to be remembered, synced, exported or deleted?
Which consequences of loss, error or access revocation are unacceptable?
common_topics.applies_when: When the result reads, creates or stores data. Review privacy even for minimal context.

common_topics.label: External actions, risk and owner participation
common_topics.why: Separates preparation from the exact external effect authorized.
questions: Which external actions are in scope: account changes, messages, publication, payments or service launch?
Which specific actions require your participation or a separate decision?
How should work stop, roll back and reconcile the actual result after interruption?
common_topics.applies_when: When external effects are possible. Reuse an exact valid grant.

common_topics.label: Host, available capabilities and handoff
common_topics.why: Makes execution and return of the actual result feasible.
questions: Where must the result operate, where do you manage it, and where should the package return?
Which hosts, tools, accounts and target devices have already been verified?
How should work move to another environment, and what should the recipient verify?
common_topics.applies_when: When tools, installation, execution or handoff are needed. Verify the actual operation in the named service.

common_topics.label: Acceptance, evidence and independent review
common_topics.why: Defines what demonstrates completion of the current stage.
questions: What behavior or artifact will you inspect to accept the result?
Which errors, boundary conditions and recovery situations must be demonstrated?
Where do we need an independent expert, real user, device or post-launch observation?
common_topics.applies_when: Always. Verify domain quality and actual use independently of schema or checklist checks.

common_topics.label: Unknowns, research and future decisions
common_topics.why: Resolves material uncertainty through research and recommendations.
questions: Which decisions are still open and need research and a recommendation?
Which researched options fit your criteria, and do you accept the recommended option?
Which future parameters can be decided later, within what limits and by which milestone?
decisions: Deferred owner, baseline or range, due point and reopening condition
common_topics.applies_when: Always. Resolve every applicable material unknown before approving the execution plan.

topics.label: Skill, agent or end product
topics.why: The constructor builds the method needed for the work. A full downstream project has its own scope.
questions: What recurring work should the skill perform, and for whom?
Are you asking for a new specialization, a family, a change to an existing skill, or execution of an already approved scope?
topics.applies_when: Always. Reuse discovery from an accepted exact Foundry handoff.

topics.label: Existing specialists and the package to change
topics.why: Inventory existing capability before defining new work.
questions: Which installed skills or agents can cover all or part of this task?
Which exact source, version, blueprint, inherited IDs and accepted originals must carry forward?
topics.applies_when: Before creating or refining a specialization. Verify what is actually available.

topics.label: Original tasks and desired change
topics.why: Real examples establish domain scope and acceptance.
questions: What real input will the skill receive, and what result will a person or downstream stage use?
Which example and counterexample distinguish a good result from an unacceptable simplification?
topics.applies_when: For a new or materially changed method.

topics.label: Domain, methods and sources
topics.why: Specialization requires an exact method suited to the domain.
questions: Which concepts, entities, roles, rules, states and dependencies define the work?
Which current primary sources and methods support a reliable result, and where do they apply?
topics.applies_when: When the domain is unfamiliar or the sources have changed.

topics.label: Compare solution forms
topics.why: Choose the smallest sufficient solution for the actual problem.
questions: Which existing process, deterministic automation, specialist skill, agent or application can achieve the goal?
Which route best meets the requirements, cost, authority and accuracy, and what are the strongest objections?
topics.applies_when: Before choosing an architecture.

topics.label: Scenario and variant classes
topics.why: Identify material requirements beyond the normal path.
questions: Which first-use, normal, peak, boundary, incomplete, failure, retry, cold-return and end-of-service scenarios apply?
Which locale, platform, channel, permission or scale variants change rules or outputs?
topics.applies_when: For every key output. Include additional platforms only when the work requires them.

topics.label: Actual tools and production route
topics.why: Validate the executable operation behind a tool name.
questions: Which exact operations, inputs, outputs, editable masters, runtime derivatives and checks are needed?
Which capabilities, rights, versions, costs and support limits are currently verified?
topics.applies_when: When the method uses tools, code, generation, integration or handoff.

topics.label: Single skill or justified family
topics.why: Stable work boundaries determine how many skill files are useful.
questions: Which competencies, outputs, access boundaries, long-running cycles or independent reuse justify separate skills?
Would one specialist with conditional phases provide a simpler sufficient route?
topics.applies_when: Before the blueprint. Choose phases and leads only when the work requires them.

topics.label: Stages and exact handoffs
topics.why: A downstream consumer needs a usable accepted result without reconstructing decisions.
questions: What stable artifact does each stage deliver to its consumer, and which decisions are already resolved?
What input maturity, hashes, interfaces, acceptance, failure and return route, and carry-forward material does each dependency need?
topics.applies_when: When phases or skills have distinct consumers.

topics.label: Competencies, writer and independent reviewer
topics.why: Verify who actually did the work and performed the review.
questions: Which independent outputs need specialists, and who integrates them?
Where are domain review, independent QA or an advisory group needed for a material decision, and what resources belong to each actor?
topics.applies_when: When quality needs several competencies. Identify author self-checks.

topics.label: Causal rules, state and probabilistic output
topics.why: A complete design specifies behavior and trust boundaries.
questions: Which entities, mutable fields, commands, events, formulas, units, guards, transitions and recovery rules apply?
Which results are facts, assumptions or probabilistic estimates, and when should the system abstain, fall back or involve a person?
topics.applies_when: For applicable logic. Add a database, RAG or server only when it serves a demonstrated need.

topics.label: Complete requirements and quality register
topics.why: Surface unresolved requirements before production.
questions: Does every accepted requirement have a source, priority, applicability, owner, consumer and acceptance criterion?
Which priorities, negative examples, rights and resource limits must each dependent child skill inherit?
topics.applies_when: Before approval of the skill design.

topics.label: Domain-specific package contents
topics.why: Show the user the executable method and concrete outputs.
questions: Which exact SKILL files, references, assets, scripts, schemas, cases and metadata does the accepted scope require?
For each child, what are the workflow entry and exit, production recipe, local and stage acceptance, and routes back upstream?
topics.applies_when: Before building the target skill. Require domain-specific behavior beyond a generic scaffold.

topics.label: Current architecture and later detail
topics.why: Keep any material unresolved product choice visible.
questions: Which unknowns affect triggers, scope, rules, quality, costs or effects and need a decision now?
Which numerical tuning choices or future inputs can be delegated to a stage with a baseline or range, owner, probe, due point and reopening condition?
topics.applies_when: Before the execution plan. Resolve material unknowns first.

topics.label: Specific proposal and authorization boundary
topics.why: Approval applies to the exact versioned proposal the owner reviewed.
questions: Which evidence-backed option for structure, methods and resources do you accept?
Do you approve this exact blueprint revision, target changes and production bounds for the skills?
topics.applies_when: After material questions are resolved. Reuse exact current consent or accepted parent scope.

topics.label: Executable domain method
topics.why: Each child skill must be able to perform its assigned work.
questions: How do the accepted requirements become an ordered domain algorithm, exact rules, resources and production recipes?
What inputs, prerequisites, expected outcomes, negative cases, uncertainty and failure routes, and acceptance criteria does the executor need?
topics.applies_when: After the actual build gate for the approved design is satisfied.

topics.label: Self-contained skills and inherited requirements
topics.why: Each skill should run independently from hidden paths to siblings.
questions: Which parent IDs, constraints, source lineage, rights and shared contracts must each child carry?
How should the package include required common resources by version, and how will it be tested in a clean context?
topics.applies_when: For a single skill or family. Verify that every inherited resource is actually available.

topics.label: Recipes, transformations and external effects
topics.why: Execution needs exact parameters and a way to reconcile unknown outcomes.
questions: Which actual tool bindings, supported parameters, transformations, masters, derivatives, fixtures and validators are needed?
How will timeout, retry, reconciliation, pause and resume, repair, stop and output return work within granted authority?
topics.applies_when: When generation, code, integration, long jobs or external operations are needed.

topics.label: Triggers, interaction and metadata
topics.why: The user should be able to discover and use the skill correctly.
questions: Which positive and negative triggers, required inputs, output format, entry and exit are clear to the user?
Which exact local links, commands, UI metadata and concise user instructions correspond to actual files?
topics.applies_when: For every installable child. Keep internal identifiers out of user responsibilities.

topics.label: Structure, consistency and requirement preservation
topics.why: Use each automated check within its actual proof scope.
questions: Which quick_validate, consistency, schema, reference and CLI checks apply to the exact installed sources?
Does every parent requirement have a child assignment, consumer and due evidence? Do any instructions conflict?
topics.applies_when: Before saving target sources. Use an existing adequate validator where available.

topics.label: Independent domain forward test
topics.why: An original task shows whether the method can produce the intended result.
questions: Which bounded positive and negative cases will another actor run from the original request without the diagnosis or expected answer?
Which relevant cases test missing approval, critical unknowns, self-review, stale dependencies and cold return?
topics.applies_when: For material complexity and as required by the accepted evidence plan.

topics.label: Scoped acceptance, repair and evidence reuse
topics.why: Fix the identified defect while preserving existing behavior.
questions: Which findings affect which exact requirements or artifacts, and how?
Which evidence is stale or still valid, who retests, and when does diagnosis need to change instead of repeating the same attempt?
topics.applies_when: After a finding or a change to a shared dependency.

topics.label: Current host and supported installation
topics.why: A real installation has an exact target and receipt.
questions: Which host, account and catalog should expose the skill, and what supported save or installation route is available?
What actual prerequisites, costs, permissions or owner actions are needed, and what is already authorized?
topics.applies_when: Before installation or export. Verify account registration separately from package creation.

topics.label: Package, readback and cold start
topics.why: The saved skill must be self-contained and discoverable.
questions: Which exact files, versions, hashes, manifests, dependencies and install, verify and rollback instructions must be delivered?
How will a fresh session read the saved sources, find the stable trigger and complete the first useful bounded task?
topics.applies_when: For each separately installable skill. Install the skills the intended stage actually needs.

topics.label: Another constructor and parent handoff
topics.why: Return the constructed result to the owner of the accepted intent.
questions: Which child sources, inherited IDs, exact outputs and evidence, gaps and next action does the parent or user need?
Does the existing request include the final product, or is delivery of the method the stopping point?
topics.applies_when: When Foundry or another bounded component requests the skill.

topics.label: Exact change and preservation of current requirements
topics.why: Carry forward accepted obligations even when the new request does not repeat them.
questions: Which specific defect, new competency or host or tool change needs to be addressed?
Which sources, triggers, rules, assets, permissions and outputs remain accepted and must be preserved?
topics.applies_when: For updates, repairs, narrowing or expansion of an existing specialization.

topics.label: Dependencies, migration and scoped approval
topics.why: A material change and a routine repair have different decision boundaries.
questions: Which child contracts, handoff consumers, schemas, recipes and installed versions does the change affect?
Does it materially change the goal, architecture, rights, resources or effects, and which specific decision is due?
decisions: Material approval delta vs authorized repair
topics.applies_when: Before dependent changes or replacement of an installed version.

topics.label: Regression and verification of the saved version
topics.why: A source change must prove preservation and new behavior within applicable scope.
questions: Which existing cases and new negative cases test the change?
Which checks and evidence must be refreshed, and how will we verify the exact saved version and rollback?
topics.applies_when: After implementing the change and before declaring readiness.

topics.label: Resume from the actual sources
topics.why: Restore accepted scope and reuse valid existing answers.
questions: Which actual blueprint, sources, installed revision, approvals, evidence and checkpoint are current?
Which jobs, source changes, unresolved effects, resources and stopping conditions need reconciliation before continuation?
topics.applies_when: After pause, handoff or a host change. Prefill available answers with provenance.

topics.label: Reopen affected work
topics.why: Carry forward accepted independent work when resuming.
questions: What changed since the checkpoint, and which decisions or evidence are stale?
What is the next due gate, and which material unknowns must be resolved before executing its dependent work?
topics.applies_when: Before the next dependent action.
